title: Introduce lineage-aware trace IDs and SLO attribution for analytics transform pipeline
creator: Aisha Karim
description: Add lineage-aware trace identifiers and per-stage SLO attribution across our analytics ingestion and transform pipeline so we can deterministically map SLO breaches to the pipeline stage (ingest, transform, enrichment, materialization) and tenant. This enables accurate alerting, quicker RCA, and cost-aware sampling strategies for high-cardinality tenants.
background: Current observability for analytics focuses on aggregate SLIs (ingest success rate, pipeline lag) and distributed traces that lack consistent lineage keys across transform stages. When an SLO breach occurs we often see noisy signals and cannot easily attribute the failure to a specific transform or tenant because spans use ephemeral IDs and sampling removes early-stage context.
problem_statement: We need deterministic attribution for SLOs so that when downstream dashboards or feature flags degrade, we can: 1) identify the precise transform stage causing the issue, 2) surface the affected tenant(s) and routes, and 3) avoid noisy paging by having high-fidelity traces for high-risk tenants while keeping telemetry volume controlled.
goals: Propagate a stable lineage_trace_id across all processing stages for each analytics event or batch
Define per-stage SLIs (p50/p95 transform latency, completeness %, error rate) and map them to tenant scoped SLOs
Implement adaptive trace sampling that biases for lineage health (keep full traces for lineage_trace_id flagged as anomalous or high-spend tenants)
Add dashboards and alert rules that attribute failures to pipeline stages and tenant groups
Keep additional telemetry cost under a 10% estimated increase for observability spend
success_metrics: Mean time to identify root stage for SLO breaches reduced from 3h to <30m
Fraction of SLO incidents with tenant-stage attribution > 90%
Increase in high-fidelity traces for flagged tenants without exceeding +10% telemetry cost
Automated alerts with correct stage attribution for >= 95% of simulated failures in the canary suite
proposed_solution: Introduce a lineage_trace_id (UUID v4) assigned at the earliest safe point (edge ingestion proxy or first consumer) and carry it as a first-class context field through Kafka messages, transform jobs, and materializers
Standardize tracing headers: X-Redwood-Lineage, x-redwood-tenant, x-redwood-route to be injected and respected by all services
Enhance span tags to include stage=ingest|transform|enrich|materialize, tenant_id, route_id, batch_id, and transform_version

Implement deterministic sampling rules in the trace collector: always retain full traces if lineage_trace_id is in anomaly list, retain full traces for top 0.5% spend tenants, otherwise use 1% baseline with reservoir sampling for early-stage spans
Extend existing SLO evaluation job to compute stage-level SLIs per tenant and feed results into a SLO attribution store
Create dashboards that pivot by stage and tenant cohort and playbooks for automated rollback/mitigation (e.g., pause enrichment, fall back to cached aggregates)
design_decisions: lineage_trace_id is immutable and attached to every event/batch; we will not reuse request_id for lineage to avoid conflation with API layer retries
Use Kafka message header for propagation where possible to avoid schema changes to payloads; legacy consumers must read header and backfill to message body if required
Sampling strategy will be configurable via console feature flag per environment, with a default conservative policy in prod
Stage-level SLOs will be computed at 1m and 5m windows to balance noise and responsiveness
implementation_tasks: ENG: Add lineage_trace_id generation to edge-proxy and ingestion lambda (Mateo)
ENG: Update Kafka client libraries to propagate headers and the tracing middleware to map headers -> span context (Harpreet)
ENG: Modify transform runners to include lineage_trace_id in all emitted spans and logs (Sadia)
ENG: Update trace-collector to support adaptive sampling rules and reservoir for flagged lineage ids (Observability infra)
ENG: Extend SLO evaluation pipeline to perform per-stage aggregation and write attribution records to metrics-store (Aisha)
PM: Draft dashboard requirements and runbook triggers (Evan)
DES: Wireframe dashboard drilldowns for tenant-stage SLOs and quick actions (Amira)
QA: Create synthetic regression suite that injects stage-specific failures and validates attribution (QA team)
SEC: Review header propagation for PII leakage risk and ensure tenant_id is hashed where necessary (Security)
OPS: Cost projection and budget alerting for telemetry spend (Finance/Infra)
Release: Feature-flag rollouts: dev -> staging -> small-prod cohort -> all-prod
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): Implement header propagation + local tracing changes; smoke tests (2 weeks)
Stage 2 (staging): Enable lineage IDs and enhanced spans for staging runs; run synthetic failure suite (1 week)
Stage 3 (canary prod): Enable for 5% of tenants (prefer high-spend and low-risk cohorts); monitor telemetry cost and false positives (2 weeks)
Stage 4 (full prod): Gate by cost telemetry acceptance and security approval; enable default sampling for remaining tenants
monitoring_dashboard_requirements: Overview: pipeline-level SLIs and telemetry cost impact
Drilldown: tenant cohort view with stage p95 latency, error rate, and completeness
Trace search: filter by lineage_trace_id, tenant_id, stage, and batch_id
Heatmap: rate of stage degradations over time with links to last trace and related logs
Sampling stats: fraction retained by sampling rule and reservoir utilization
runbook_and_alerting: Alert: stage_p95_latency > threshold for > 3 consecutive 1m windows -> page on-call and create incident with correlated lineage ids
Alert: completeness drop > 5% for a tenant cohort -> auto-open investigation ticket and run quick rollback mitigation (disable enrichment)
Runbook steps: reproduce using synthetic trace generator -> attach lineage_trace_id -> check transform logs -> escalate to transform owners
Post-incident: record stage attribution and update SLO burn graphs; if repeat failures attributed to same transform, schedule prioritization
risks_and_mitigation: High-cardinality tenant identifiers may spike telemetry costs -> mitigate with hashed tenant_id in traces and reservoir sampling
Legacy consumers not reading headers -> provide sidecar that copies header into message body for backward compatibility
Security/PII risk with tenant identifiers -> coordinate with Security to pseudonymize or hash tenant_id as needed
Increased trace volume may impact collector performance -> incremental rollout and rate limiting at collector ingress
notes: We should align on a minimal lineage_schema before implementation to avoid multiple incompatible ids
Consider exposing lineage_trace_id in console logs UI for customer support debugging
Budget estimate: initial telemetry increase ~6-9% in canary, refine after sampling thresholds tuned
